title.en: Plot only where the function is defined

summary: Restrict the sampled domain, handle poles and undefined regions explicitly, and state the window and clamping used.
objective: Prevent a surface plot from inventing geometry where the function has none.
applies_when: A function surface, field or contour set is generated from an expression.
The function has poles, branch cuts, or regions where it is undefined.
The viewer can pan, zoom or change parameters.
intent_signals: it blows up near the origin
example_prompts: Plot the surface and handle the pole sensibly.
Show the function only where it is defined.
negative_signals: Smooth bounded functions on a fixed domain, where the issue does not arise.
Sampled data sets, which have their own coverage question rather than a domain question.
not_for: Smooth bounded functions on a fixed domain, where the issue does not arise.
Sampled data sets, which have their own coverage question rather than a domain question.

principles: A mesh generator will happily connect a huge value to a small one and draw a wall. That wall is a rendering artefact, not a feature of the function, and viewers read it as geometry.
Undefined is different from large. A region outside the domain should be absent, not drawn at a clamped height, or the plot asserts values that do not exist.
Clamping is a legitimate choice but it is a display transformation, so the clamp value must be shown or the vertical axis becomes meaningless.
The window is part of the claim: a function looks completely different over different ranges, and a viewer who cannot see the window cannot interpret the shape.
implementation: Evaluate with explicit domain checks and mark samples as undefined rather than substituting a number.
Break the mesh at undefined samples and across poles instead of interpolating through them, so the surface has real holes.
If clamping, display the clamp threshold and mark clamped regions visually so they are not read as flat plateaux.
Show the axis ranges and the sample resolution on the artifact, and update them when the viewer pans or zooms.
Give a stated behaviour for parameter values that make the function degenerate, rather than leaving the mesh generator to improvise.
observable_checks: Zoom towards a pole and confirm the surface breaks rather than forming a smooth wall.
Check that undefined regions are absent rather than flat.
Confirm the displayed axis range and clamp value match what is drawn.
Increase the sample resolution and confirm features persist rather than appearing or disappearing.

creative_affordances: Artistic treatment of the surface, including colour mapping and lighting, is unconstrained.
A deliberately clipped view can be the clearest presentation when the clipping is visible.
known_limits: Authored plotting guidance; no runtime plot has been generated or inspected for this record.
It does not prescribe a sampling algorithm or an adaptive refinement strategy.
